title_seen: NN2FPGA: Optimizing CNN Inference on FPGAs With Binary Integer Programming
work_done: HLS compiler (nn2fpga) that maps skip-connection CNNs (ResNet8, ResNet20, MobileNetV2) to static layer-pipelined dataflow accelerators, with reduced skip-buffering and a binary-integer-programming DSE that assigns FPGA resources per layer.
advantages: Reports 3x-7x throughput over prior HLS work on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet; MobileNetV2 on ZCU102 reaches 2115 FPS, about 10% above a hand-optimized RTL design.
disadvantages: Throughput-oriented static dataflow design; the abstract reports throughput only and makes no latency-predictability or cycle-exactness claim.
relevance: Closest prior work: custom INT8 ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 on the same KV260 board (per the earlier t5 full-text pass); the performance bar V3 is compared against.
read_locator: abstract (OpenAlex record of the TCAD version)
notes: KV260 ResNet20 numbers (7601 FPS, 0.318 ms, 6.10 W) come from the earlier t5 full-text pass, not re-read here; arXiv 2309.15631 preprint has different clock/power, cite TCAD.

title_seen: An Exploration of State-of-the-Art Automation Frameworks for FPGA-Based DNN Acceleration
work_done: Compares FINN (dataflow) and Vitis AI DPU (overlay) on the same FPGA hardware and DNN by extending the FINN flow, plus Jetson Nano and Core i7 reference platforms.
advantages: Same-hardware, same-model comparison of the two Xilinx frameworks; FINN accelerator beats the Vitis AI one by 8.4x latency, 3.0x throughput and 3.3x power efficiency.
disadvantages: Covers only the two Xilinx frameworks; the abstract notes dataflow designs scale poorly with DNN size.
relevance: Direct baseline context: DPU vs custom dataflow on a K26-based board, the same DPU baseline V3 uses.
notes: Earlier t5 full-text pass: K26 SoM board, ResNet-8 CIFAR-10, FINN latency computed from Verilog-simulation cycles. IEEE PDF blocked to our fetch this time.

title_seen: A High-Performance CNN Processor Based on FPGA for MobileNets
work_done: DPU-lineage MobileNet processor with separate Conv (pointwise) and Dwcv (depthwise) engines in a layer pipeline and Channel Augmentation for the first layer; 8-bit, on ZU2 (430 MHz) and ZU9 (333 MHz).
advantages: MobileNetV2 ImageNet at 205.3 fps on ZU2 and 809.8 fps on ZU9 at 68.1% top-1 (Table V); configurable core sizes (DPU S 212 DSP, DPU L 2070 DSP, Table III).
disadvantages: No power numbers in the tables read; top-1 68.1% is below the 72% float reference; MobileNetV2+SSD deployment stated as still in progress.
relevance: AMD/Xilinx DPU lineage on ZU+ with a dedicated depthwise engine: prior art for V3's depthwise mode and the DPU baseline.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. III-D, Sec. IV, Tables III-VI, Sec. V
notes: Read from a course-hosted copy of the IEEE version.

title_seen: DNNVM: End-to-End Compiler Leveraging Heterogeneous Optimizations on FPGA-Based CNN Accelerators
work_done: Full-stack compiler for an ISA-driven FPGA CNN accelerator (Xilinx/DeePhi DPU style): XGraph IR, heuristic subgraph-isomorphism fusion, pipeline/data-layout search, assembler and runtime; evaluated on ZU2 and ZU9 at 330 MHz.
advantages: Up to 1.26x throughput from the heterogeneous optimizations; ResNet50 at 1.38 TOPs/s and VGG at 2.82 TOPs/s / 123.7 GOPs/s/W on ZU9.
disadvantages: Throughput-oriented (TOPs/s) results; ImageNet-scale networks only; compiler for one custom ISA accelerator.
relevance: Compiler side of the DPU baseline: per-layer scheduling/fusion for an instruction-driven ZU+ accelerator, contrast to V3's exact per-layer cycle model.
read_locator: arXiv v2: abstract, Secs. 1 and 3 (grep-level); TCAD version abstract (OpenAlex)
notes: Published TCAD version not read in full; arXiv v2 read. | Integrator 2026-10-07: basis set to abstract (full text only keyword-checked, not read).

title_seen: A High-Throughput Full-Dataflow MobileNetv2 Accelerator on Edge FPGA
work_done: Full-dataflow INT8 MobileNetV2 accelerator: improved full-integer quantization, tunable activation-weight imbalance transfer, parallelism-adjustable components, deeper-FIFO residual connections, and per-layer compute/memory allocation.
advantages: 1910 FPS on ZCU102 (1.8x over prior work) with 72.98% top-1 at 8-bit, the highest among the MobileNetV2 accelerators it compares.
disadvantages: Single network (MobileNetV2) design point on a large ZU9 device; full-dataflow mapping is network-specific.
relevance: State of the art for MobileNet-style INT8 on ZU+; contrast to V3's single-array, layer-sequential approach.

title_seen: FINN-R: An End-to-End Deep-Learning Framework for Fast Exploration of Quantized Neural Networks
work_done: Second-generation FINN: end-to-end tool that generates customized quantized inference engines (dataflow or multi-layer offload) with resource-cost and performance models; evaluated on PYNQ-Z1, Ultra96 (XCZU3EG) and AWS F1.
advantages: Up to 50 TOp/s on AWS F1 and 5 TOp/s on embedded devices; on Ultra96 CNV-6 runs at 300 MHz (results table).
disadvantages: Targets reduced-precision (binary/few-bit) networks, not INT8; the CIFAR-10 CNV and YOLO models differ from ResNet/MobileNet.
relevance: FINN dataflow framework on ZU+ (Ultra96): the main open-source custom-accelerator alternative to the DPU.
read_locator: arXiv: abstract, Sec. 5 platform table and results table (grep-level)
notes: Integrator 2026-10-07: basis set to abstract (full text only keyword-checked, not read).

title_seen: Dynamic Dataflow Scheduling and Computation Mapping Techniques for Efficient Depthwise Separable Convolution Acceleration
work_done: Adaptive row-based dataflow scheduling and adaptive computation mapping for depthwise separable convolution accelerators, evaluated on six DSC-based lightweight CNNs and implemented for MobileNetV2 on ZCU102.
advantages: At least 50.4% smaller on-chip buffer and 1.18x convolution performance in simulation; 381.7 fps MobileNetV2 on ZCU102, 1.43x the reference design.
disadvantages: Buffer/performance gains are simulation results; board result is for MobileNetV2 only.
relevance: Per-layer adaptive scheduling for depthwise layers on ZU+: prior art for V3's depthwise mode and per-layer mode choice.

title_seen: RADAR: An Efficient FPGA-based ResNet Accelerator with Data-aware Reordering of Processing Sequences
work_done: ResNet-18 accelerator IP that reorders each layer's computation sequence to maximize on-chip-memory reuse and uses a shared buffer for skip-connection layers, implemented on ZCU102.
advantages: 446.9 GOPS and 64.9 GOPS/W with less DRAM access and higher OCM and processor utilization.
disadvantages: Single network (ResNet-18) on a large ZU9 device; abstract gives no frame rate or latency.
relevance: ZU+ ResNet accelerator handling skip connections with limited on-chip memory, comparable to V3's residual handling.
notes: New (not in earlier t5 list). Smaller venue (JSTS).

title_seen: DeepDive: An Integrative Algorithm/Architecture Co-Design for Deep Separable Convolutional Neural Networks
work_done: Co-design framework for depthwise separable CNNs on edge FPGAs: heterogeneous compute units in synthesizable C++, FPGA-aware training and online channel-wise low-bit quantization, run on ZCU102.
advantages: 47.4 FPS/W (MobileNet-V2) and 233.3 FPS/W (compact EfficientNet); 2.2x/1.51x over Jetson Nano modes and 2.27x/37.25x over two FPGA designs.
disadvantages: Uses low-bit (about 3-6 bit) quantization rather than INT8; results given as FPS/W.
relevance: MobileNet-style accelerator on ZU+ with heterogeneous units for depthwise layers; contrast point for V3's MobileNet workload.
read_locator: abstract (OpenAlex record); arXiv text checked for board/bit-width only

title_seen: Synetgy: Algorithm-hardware Co-design for ConvNet Accelerators on Embedded FPGAs
work_done: Co-designs DiracDeltaNet (1x1 convs plus shift operations, 1-bit weights / 4-bit activations) and an HLS accelerator on Ultra96 at 250 MHz.
advantages: 88.2% top-5 ImageNet at 96.5 FPS; power measured with a power monitor (5.3 W idle PL, 5.5 W max).
disadvantages: Network is custom (not ResNet/MobileNet) and ultra-low precision, so it is not directly comparable to INT8 designs.
relevance: Early ZU+ (Ultra96) embedded CNN accelerator with board power; context for board-level power reporting.
notes: Integrator 2026-10-07: basis set to abstract (full text only keyword-checked, not read).

title_seen: HAO: Hardware-aware Neural Architecture Optimization for Efficient Inference
work_done: Joint NAS, quantization and accelerator-configuration search using integer programming and a subgraph-based FPGA latency model plus an accuracy predictor, targeting a ZU3EG device.
advantages: Searched network reaches 72.5% top-1 ImageNet at 50 fps, 60% faster than MnasNet and 135% faster than FBNet at similar accuracy.
disadvantages: Latency comes from a model used for search; the network is a searched MobileNet-like model, not a standard one.
relevance: Uses an analytic FPGA latency model for design search on ZU+; contrast to V3's exact cycle model.
notes: Could overlap with an NAS/co-design category.

title_seen: Benchmarking edge computing devices for grape bunches and trunks detection using accelerated object detection single shot multibox deep learning models
work_done: Benchmarks RetinaNet ResNet-50 detection on Jetson Nano/TX2 GPUs, Coral TPU and DPU on ZCU104 and Kria KV260.
advantages: FPGA DPU platforms were fastest (14-25 FPS vs 3-5 FPS for GPUs) with similar detection quality (F1 about 70%, mAP about 60%).
disadvantages: Detection workload with off-the-shelf DPU only; GPUs and TPU were the most power-efficient (about 5 W).
relevance: Independent KV260/ZCU104 DPU measurements for the ResNet-50 family; context for the DPU baseline.

title_seen: An Experimental Study of Reduced-Voltage Operation in Modern FPGAs for Neural Network Acceleration
work_done: Undervolting study of CNN accelerators (DNNDK DPU, B4096 cores) on three ZCU102 boards with five ImageNet CNNs including ResNet50, with on-chip rails monitored via PMBus.
advantages: More than 3x GOPs/W gain from undervolting, 2.6x of it from removing the vendor voltage guardband; frequency underscaling avoids accuracy loss.
disadvantages: Main topic is voltage/reliability, not accelerator design; below-guardband operation costs accuracy.
relevance: DPU on ZU+ with rail-level power measurement; methodology reference for V3's power reporting.
